name: Nicholas A. Langworthy
signature: Energy and Commerce Republican who wants one national AI standard: urged Commerce to target New York's RAISE Act as overregulation, while backing kids-online-safety, deepfake and AI-child-exploitation bills.

notable_quote.text: We cannot allow a patchwork of burdensome state regulations to weaken our competitive edge, nor can we afford to let Communist China dictate the global rules of the road.

groups: House Energy and Commerce Republican Privacy Working Group (member, 2025)
House Committee on Energy and Commerce, Subcommittee on Energy (member)

data_centers.summary: Langworthy treats rising demand from data centers as a reason to build more power plants and speed up permitting, not as a reason to slow data centers. He has not been found commenting on Gov. Hochul's 2026 data center pause.

evidence.title: Wellsville Sun: Borrello, Langworthy and Molitor call on Hochul to repower the idle NRG plant in Dunkirk
evidence.quote: You cannot remove dependable energy from the grid while demand is growing and expect costs to fall or reliability to improve.
evidence.what_it_shows: He named data centers, along with manufacturing, as drivers of rising electricity demand and argued the answer is more generation, not less demand.

evidence.title: Roll call 356: Yea on the SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), federal permitting reform
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted for a permitting-reform bill widely tied to speeding up energy and data center construction.

evidence.title: Press release: Langworthy and Schrier introduce the FLOWS Act to modernize hydropower permitting
evidence.what_it_shows: Another supply-side, cut-red-tape energy bill; it shows his general build-more-power approach rather than a data center position.

ai_risk.summary: Mixed but leaning light touch. He backs targeted protections for kids, deepfake victims and AI child-exploitation cases, yet he asked Commerce to treat New York's frontier-AI safety law (the RAISE Act) as harmful overregulation and wants innovation-first national standards to stay ahead of China.

evidence.title: Letter with Rep. Gabe Evans to Commerce Secretary Lutnick flagging Colorado SB 205 and New York's RAISE Act as AI overregulation
evidence.quote: The United States is best positioned to establish strong, innovation-driven standards that protect consumers, safeguard children, and promote economic growth.
evidence.what_it_shows: He asked the administration to list New York's AI safety law among burdensome state rules, framing AI policy around innovation and competition with China.

evidence.title: Statement on House passage of the Kids Internet and Digital Safety Act (KIDS Act)
evidence.quote: Families deserve real tools to shield children from online predators, addictive algorithms, scams, dangerous and illegal products, explicit content, and the emerging risks posed by AI.
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports specific, kid-focused rules that include AI risks.

evidence.title: Sponsor: Child Exploitation and Artificial Intelligence Expert Commission Act of 2024 (H.R. 8005, 118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: His own AI bill created a study commission on AI-generated child abuse material rather than new binding rules.

evidence.title: Press release: Langworthy introduces legislation to combat the use of AI to create child sexual abuse material
evidence.quote: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence poses unique challenges for protecting our children now and in the future as technology evolves
evidence.what_it_shows: He sees AI as a real threat to children and wants law enforcement tools to keep up.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Preventing Deepfakes of Intimate Images Act (H.R. 1941)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports criminal penalties for sharing AI-made sexual deepfakes.

evidence.title: House Oversight hearing wrap-up: Federal Government Use of Artificial Intelligence Poses Promise, Peril
evidence.quote: Do you agree that the public has right to know for what purposes AI is being used by the federal agencies and that it’s important that these inventories are done consistently, completely and accurately
evidence.what_it_shows: He pressed for transparency about government AI use and raised concern that criminals will exploit AI.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Federal A.I. Governance and Transparency Act of 2024 (H.R. 7532, 118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed public reporting on how federal agencies use AI.

tech_regulation.summary: Langworthy favors targeted rules on Big Tech: kids' online safety, app store competition, foreign robocalls, data brokers and forcing TikTok away from Chinese control. He has not called for break-ups or repealing Section 230.

evidence.title: Statement on House passage of the Kids Internet and Digital Safety Act (KIDS Act)
evidence.quote: This bill gives parents more control, strengthens privacy protections for children, updates outdated online safety laws, and holds Big Tech accountable for putting profits ahead of our kids’ well-being.
evidence.what_it_shows: He celebrated a kids-online-safety law in explicitly anti-Big-Tech terms.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: App Store Freedom Act (H.R. 3209)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports forcing Apple and Google to allow outside app stores.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Foreign Robocall Elimination Act (H.R. 6152)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a specific crackdown on scam robocalls from abroad.

evidence.title: Press release and floor speech: Langworthy votes to force TikTok to cut ties with the Chinese Communist Party
evidence.quote: This is a significant national security risk as TikTok’s parent company, ByteDance, is owned by the Chinese Communist Party
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed a forced divestiture of TikTok on national security and data-privacy grounds.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Child Online Safety Modernization Act of 2023 (H.R. 5182, 118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports stronger reporting duties for platforms on child abuse material.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Protecting Military Servicemembers' Data Act of 2023 (H.R. 6573, 118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports limits on data brokers selling troops' personal data to hostile countries.

evidence.title: IAPP: House Republicans organize a privacy working group (Langworthy named a member)
evidence.what_it_shows: He sits on the Energy and Commerce GOP group drafting a national consumer privacy bill.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Protecting Speech from Government Interference Act (H.R. 140, 118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: His Big Tech concerns also include government pressure on platforms to remove posts, a conservative free-speech angle.

preemption.summary: Langworthy wants one national AI rule. In February 2026 he and Rep. Gabe Evans asked Commerce to list New York's RAISE Act and Colorado's AI law as burdensome state laws under President Trump's preemption executive order, calling for uniform federal standards.

evidence.title: Letter with Rep. Gabe Evans to Commerce Secretary Lutnick on AI overregulation in Colorado and New York
evidence.quote: We cannot allow a patchwork of burdensome state regulations to weaken our competitive edge, nor can we afford to let Communist China dictate the global rules of the road.
evidence.what_it_shows: He urged the administration to include his own state's AI safety law in the Commerce report that the December 2025 executive order uses to target state AI laws, and called uniform federal standards essential.

evidence.title: Roll call 145: Yea on House passage of H.R. 1, which then included the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted for the full reconciliation bill while it carried the state AI-law moratorium; this was a vote on the whole bill, so it is weak evidence on its own.

china_chips.summary: No public position found on AI chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China as of Sept 2026. He backs tax credits for building chip factories in the United States and is hawkish on Chinese apps like TikTok, but that is not the same question.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: BASIC Act (H.R. 3204), semiconductor manufacturing tax credit
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports domestic chip-factory incentives; neutral on export controls.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: STAR Act of 2025 (H.R. 802)
evidence.what_it_shows: Another domestic chip manufacturing tax credit; neutral on export controls.

evidence.title: Press release and floor speech on forcing TikTok to cut ties with the Chinese Communist Party
evidence.what_it_shows: Shows a China-tech hawk posture on apps and data, but he has not spoken on chip exports.

Read langworthy.house.gov press index pages 0-8 and archived AI/energy releases, the Evans-Langworthy Lutnick letter release (found on gabeevans.house.gov after Google News link decoding was rate-limited), Wellsville Sun Dunkirk article, Oversight 2023 hearing wrap-up, IAPP privacy working group piece, govtrack roll calls h145 and h356. Not found: any statement on Hochul's July 2026 data center pause or on the Ratepayer Protection Act markup he sat through as an E&C member; any chip export control statement. His Energy Choice Act, BUSES Act and Dietary Supplement Regulatory Uniformity Act all preempt state rules in other areas, consistent with the AI preemption stance but not counted as AI evidence.

name: Claudia Tenney
signature: Semiconductor tax-credit champion (sponsor of the BASIC Act) and China-tech hawk who backs deepfake-victim bills; little public record on broader AI safety or data centers.

notable_quote.text: Our laws must keep pace with emerging technology and make clear that exploitation and abuse, whether online or offline, will not be tolerated.

groups: House Big Tech Censorship and Data Task Force (House Republican task force, appointed 2021)
House Election Integrity Caucus (founder and chair)

data_centers.summary: No public statement found on data centers as of Sept 2026, even though the $19.5 billion Stream/STAMP project sits in her district's Genesee County. Her energy statements blame Albany's climate mandates for high bills and never mention data centers; she voted for federal permitting reform.

evidence.title: Roll call 356: Yea on the SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), federal permitting reform
evidence.what_it_shows: She voted for permitting reform often tied to energy and data center buildout, but the bill is not specific to data centers.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: DEFIANCE Act of 2025 (H.R. 3562)

evidence.title: Cosponsor: bill to codify Executive Order 14319 on preventing 'woke AI' in the federal government (H.R. 4873)

evidence.title: Cosponsor: DETECT Act of 2025 (H.R. 4974), study of AI to catch tax fraud

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Child Exploitation and Artificial Intelligence Expert Commission Act of 2024 (H.R. 8005, 118th)

tech_regulation.summary: Tenney favors targeted action against specific tech harms, especially Chinese-controlled apps like TikTok and AI deepfakes. evidence.title: Cosponsor: Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (H.R. 7521, 118th), the TikTok divest-or-ban law

evidence.title: Press release: Tenney joins effort to advance the DEFIANCE Act

preemption.summary: No statement found on whether Washington should override state AI laws. She voted for the May 2025 House version of H.R. 1 that carried the state AI-law moratorium, but that was a vote on the whole budget bill and does not show a position on preemption itself.
